name: Leatherworker
summary: A Universal World Class any character may take regardless of their class. It levels through active use — skinning, curing and crafting — turning what a fight leaves on the ground into satchels, cloaks, barding and armour, from deer hide to dragonhide.
_thresholds_note: Herbalist's curve, kept deliberately: the mastery awards in rules/worldclass.py are shared across tracks, so the same MP arithmetic that set 25/65/50/100 there sets it here. The dip at level 4 is the herbalist file's documented intent — each high-tier piece is a larger undertaking, so fewer of them make a level — and it holds for a breastplate exactly as it held for an elixir. Do not 'fix' it in one file and not the other; that is the stale-copy bug CLAUDE.md warns about, so if it ever changes, change both.
_deeds_note: Same shape as the herbalist's deed, for the same measured reason: a deed that requires a level-5 method can never open the gate to level 5. The deed is the material, not the method — successfully working legendary hide into anything is the proof, and masterwork tooling is the mastery that follows it. A Leatherworker 4 reaches legendary hide the way the refusals allow: with a legendary-capable tannin and a chain of methods learned by 4, since nothing below `tool` is gated at 5.

legendary-hide.note: Any successful piece worked from legendary hide, however it was reached.

levels.note: Rawhide work: skin the beast in the field, flense and salt-cure the hide, cut and stitch cured rawhide into cords, wraps, sheaths and simple satchels. The clock starts at the skinning — a green hide is refuse in two days.
True leather. Tanning binds the hide for good — it will never spoil again — and oiling keeps it leather instead of board. Monster hides open up: winter wolf, dire boar, the shells and scaled things.
Coloured and lined work: dyed leathers that hold their colour, fur-lined cloaks and boots built as two hides working together.
Cuir bouilli — leather boiled in wax until it sets like thin steel. The hardening station is where leather stops being clothing and starts being armour.
Masterwork tooling: the ornament, fit and finish that makes a piece masterwork — and dragonhide work, which accepts nothing less.

method_descriptions.skin: Takes the hide off a fallen creature in the field. This happens over a carcass, not at the bench — every hide on the bench already went through it, and the spoilage clock started when it did.
method_descriptions.flense: Scrapes fat and flesh from the inside of a green hide over the beam. Flesh left on the hide putrefies under the salt, so this comes before curing or tanning.
method_descriptions.cure: Salts a green hide to stop the spoilage clock. Cured rawhide keeps indefinitely but is not yet leather: it goes stiff, and soaking softens it back toward spoiling.
method_descriptions.cut: Cuts panels, straps and pieces to pattern. Straps are cut work and nothing more; everything assembled is cut before it is stitched.
method_descriptions.stitch: Sews cut pieces into a finished thing with thread, sinew or gut. Only cured or tanned hide takes a seam — stitching a green hide sews a bag of rot.
method_descriptions.tan: Steeps a flensed hide in tannin liquor until it is leather through and through. A tanned hide never spoils, takes every later method, and is the foundation of all higher work. The tannin must be equal to the hide: bark for beasts, harsher liquors for monsters.
method_descriptions.oil: Dresses leather with oils and fats so it stays supple, sheds water and survives service. Some oils bring their own character — salamander oil keeps fire off, troll fat closes scratches overnight.
method_descriptions.dye: Colours leather in the vat. Common dyes are colour and nothing else; the rare ones carry their own qualities into the piece.
method_descriptions.line: Builds a piece as two layers — a working outer hide and an inner lining of fur or soft leather — so both hides' qualities ride in one garment.
method_descriptions.harden: Cuir bouilli: boils tanned leather in wax until it sets rigid. Hardened leather turns blades like thin steel and is the heart of leather armour. Only tanned hide survives the kettle — raw hide boils down to glue.
method_descriptions.tool: Masterwork finishing: carved, stamped and burnished ornament, exact fit, perfect edges. A tooled piece is masterwork, takes enchantment, and is the only standard dragonhide accepts.

_method_help_note: The structured half of method_descriptions: what the tooltip renders. `does` is the mechanical effect in numbers, `needs` is what must be on the bench for the method to be legal, `for` is what a player reaches for it to accomplish. Kept beside the prose rather than replacing it — the prose is the voice, this is the answer to 'what will this button do to my DC'.

skin.does: Field action, not a bench stage: puts a hide into stock with its 48-hour spoilage clock started. Contributes no potency and no DC.
skin.needs: A fallen creature in the scene, and a skinning knife. Refused at the bench — the hide there is already off the beast.
skin.for: Turning a fight into material. What the beast was decides the hide's tier.

flense.does: No potency change. Required before cure or tan on a green hide; without it those steps are refused.
flense.needs: A green hide and the fleshing beam.
flense.for: Stopping the hide putrefying under the salt. Skipping it spoils the vat, not just the piece.

cure.does: Stops the spoilage clock permanently. No potency change. +2 DC as a stage, like any other.
cure.needs: A flensed green hide and curing salt.
cure.for: Buying time. Cured rawhide keeps forever, takes a seam, and is the cheapest way to make a hide safe on the day you skinned it.

cut.does: No potency change. Assembles the `straps` pattern on its own; every other pattern is cut before it is stitched.
cut.needs: A hide that is cured or tanned, and a half-moon knife for fine work.
cut.for: Panels to pattern. The step where a hide becomes pieces of a thing.

stitch.does: No potency change. Assembles every pattern except straps — without it the chain produces a stack of panels.
stitch.needs: Thread on the bench (linen, sinew, gut), and hide that is cured or tanned. Stitching green hide is refused: it rots.
stitch.for: Making the piece exist. This is the method that finishes an ordinary garment.

tan.does: No potency change, but it is the gate on everything above: hardening, and the armour rows on the output, require tanned leather. Also ends spoilage for good.
tan.needs: A tannin within one tier of the hide — oak bark for a deer, dragonblood tannin for dragonhide — and the bark vats.
tan.for: Turning hide into leather. Nothing that matters is reachable without it.

oil.does: Potency x1.10. Some oils carry their own effect into the piece (salamander oil, resist fire 1; troll fat, self-mending).
oil.needs: An oil on the bench — neatsfoot, currier's tallow, something rendered.
oil.for: Service life, and a cheap way to buy an extra property from the oil itself.

dye.does: No potency change. Rare dyes contribute their own effects (shadow black, +1 Stealth in darkness; void dye, +2).
dye.needs: A dye on the bench and the dye vats. Mordant salts fix the rare colours permanently.
dye.for: Colour, and at the top of the ladder a genuine mechanical property.

line.does: No potency change. Both hides' effects ride in the finished piece rather than only the outer one's.
line.needs: Two hides on the bench — an outer and an inner. Refused with one.
line.for: Stacking two hides' qualities in one garment: a working outer shell over a warm or silent lining.

harden.does: Potency x1.25. Cuir bouilli — the piece sets rigid and becomes armour-grade.
harden.needs: Tanned leather (raw hide boils to glue and is refused) and a wax on the bench, in the hardening trough.
harden.for: Armour. This is where leather stops being clothing.

tool.does: Potency x1.25 and sets `masterwork` on the output — the flag the enchanter's vessel requirement reads. Must be the last method in the chain.
tool.needs: The master tannery, and a piece worth finishing. Legendary hide accepts no lesser standard.
tool.for: Masterwork. A tooled armour piece is what an enchantment gets bound to; an untooled one cannot take it.

_portable_note: The tannery is furniture. Whether a chain can be attempted is therefore partly a question about where the character is standing, which is scene state rather than sheet state — the same split the herbalist's workbench established.
